current_local_metadata.description:
Series S2 (Monitoring & Certification) of the Viridis Canon. A steward who monitors many ecosystems under one budget has lacked a first-principles rule for splitting finite monitoring power across heterogeneous sites; effort is allocated by convention. Building on the D-Score Measurement Closure Theorem and fusing it with water-filling resource allocation, this paper proves the Monitoring Water-Filling Theorem (MWT): the steward's deadweight functional is convex, so a unique optimum exists, and it is a generalized water-filling solution governed by a single broadcast monitoring shadow price λmon. Four structural laws follow: (i) optimal effort scales as P* ∝ D−1/3; (ii) no site is optimally left dark; (iii) uniform monitoring is wasteful by a power-mean factor ρ ≥ 1; (iv) a critical certification budget Pcrit marks where added budget stops buying physical certifiability. This is the eleventh self-application of the Intelligence Bound (the ‘Surveyor’).

Scope of verification. The Lean 4 proofs (Aristotle-verified, zero sorry) certify the mathematical structure, not empirical magnitudes. Working paper; not peer-reviewed.

Compute-optimal scaling laws (Kaplan et al.; Hoffmann et al., "Chinchilla") prescribe a model-size/data-size split that minimizes loss for a fixed FLOP budget, implicitly assuming the training run may take arbitrarily long wall-clock time to realize that budget. Real training is instead bound by a hard deadline: a competitive release date, a funding window, a fixed rental period on a GPU fleet. We show that once training is required to finish within a wall-clock time tau, McCandlish et al.'s gradient-noise-scale theory of the steps/examples tradeoff becomes formally an endoreversible heat engine: batch size plays the role of a throttle, the number of optimizer steps plays the role of cycle time, and there is an absolute, un-crossable wall-clock floor tau_rm floor=S_min,t_1,N below which no finite batch size — however large — can complete training. The resulting data efficiency eta(tau)equiv D_min/D_rm used(tau) takes the exact Carnot functional form eta(tau)=1-tau_rm floor/tau, with the deadline tau playing the role of a hot reservoir and tau_rm floor the role of a cold one. Pricing wall-clock time against extra data tokens and minimizing total cost yields a closed-form golden-rule deadline tau^ast=tau_rm floor+sqrtc_D D_mintau_rm floor/c_tau — a genuine Curzon–Ahlborn-flavored square-root correction, derived rather than assumed, from the same generic near-a-critical-floor optimization that produces efficiency-at-maximum-power in physical heat engines. The theorem directly explains, in direction and mechanism, a 2026 empirical finding that wall-clock-constrained optimal model size grows differently than Chinchilla's FLOP-based prediction. All results are numerically verified (21/21); for an illustrative 18-billion-parameter model the golden-rule deadline sits at approx 30 days against an approx 18-day absolute floor, at a striking approx62% Deadline Tax in extra compute.
